touches.text: Any device or machine may have a bin/ beside its code. That folder IS its list of shortcuts: add a file to add one, delete it to remove one. A shortcut is a script that calls the long form (eg `cairn superclaude` -> `cairn cc superclaude`; `cairn show temp` -> `cairn recovery show temp`), which also saves the walk from searching farther, or does work itself (eg install). Shortcuts live beside what they serve (RULE 1). `cairn foo` whose first word is not a device means `cairn cairn foo`: top-level shortcuts are the cairn device's bin/.

A new shortcut needs no watch. Most instance bins are links to their class bin, so the shortcut is reachable the moment its file lands; the build's proof is the whole guarantee. Akien 2026-11-09, answering Q#75: "why the hell would it need a heartbeat?"

help is defined once, as a root verb in the base shim, and answers exactly as `list` does: `help` is the word people type, `list` the system's word. It is readable cold (no bus, no device woken), so `cairn help` answers when nothing else is up. WHY: "help is specifically an anticipation of the behavior of the other monkeys in my species."

`cairn help` lists [all], then [operator], then [cairn], then every other device alphabetically. [all] is the verbs every device answers because the base shim defines them (help, stop, pause, ...), read from the base shim's verb table, never listed by hand.

Help below the top prints that level's own shortcuts and verbs under [<name>], alpha order, then its parent's, out to [cairn], flat, one group after another: cairn codemother inspector_gadget help  -> [inspector_gadget] ... then [codemother] ... then [cairn] ...

base shim: the base class for every shim, customized for the device it interfaces with, internal or external. Carries the panes every device has (2.3.8), the scheduler (5.9), and the [all] verbs (2.4.11.2).

conflicts.ticket_says: bin_shortcuts must read instance bin and class bin as separate directories and merge them; the two bins are not implicitly unified through symlinks
conflicts.why: Outline asserts 'Most instance bins are links to their class bin, so the shortcut is reachable the moment its file lands' — this mechanism assumes symlinks unify the bins without needing explicit separate reads. The ticket's approach either contradicts this factually (if symlinks don't exist) or adds unnecessary complexity (if they do). These cannot both be the intended architecture.
